obtained.how: the handbook itself not obtained (Internet Archive copies are borrow-only). Read instead the intermediary the paper names: FishBase's oxygen-consumption list and its per-record summary pages for Lepomis gibbosus, which cite Altman & Dittmer (eds.) 1971 as main reference and Roberts 1964 as the study

bibliography.checked_against: FishBase's reference line ('Altman, P.L. and D.S. Dittmer (eds.), 1971') and the Internet Archive catalogue records (title 'Respiration and circulation', 1971)
bibliography.note: Publisher, place and page count (FASEB, Bethesda, 930 pp.) not verified against the title page.

claims.claim: the bluegill FB4 set predicts 20–70 % more respiration than was measured in 30-g pumpkinseed at 5–25 °C (Roberts 1964, via Altman & Dittmer 1971 and FishBase; project arithmetic, one study of unknown acclimation)
claims.note: The handbook could not be read, so the values cannot be confirmed from it. FishBase's records (main ref. Altman & Dittmer 1971; Ref. Roberts, J.L., 1964) give routine oxygen consumption of 30.0-g Lepomis gibbosus as 22.9, 48.6, 72.9, 85.7 and 120.0 mg O2/kg/h at 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25 °C (activity 'routine', stress 'none specified', no acclimation given). Redoing the project arithmetic with those values (×24/10^6 → g O2/g/d) against FB4's bluegill adult row (Kitchell et al. 1974: REQ 2, RA 0.0154, RB −0.2, RQ 2.1, RTO 36, RTM 40, ACT 1; FB4 respiration equation 2 as printed in the FB4 manual, p. 14) for a 30-g fish gives model/measured ratios of 1.69, 1.21, 1.21, 1.53 and 1.57 — i.e. 21–69 % more, matching '20–70 %'. The comparison is model respiration at ACT 1 against measured routine rate.

notes: For the rewrite: the number chain is Roberts (1964) → Altman & Dittmer (1971) → FishBase → the notes. Roberts 1964 itself is the primary study and would be the one to fetch (not identified further here; FishBase gives only 'Roberts, J.L., 1964'). FishBase's '(mg/kg/h) at 20 °C' column is temperature-standardised by an unstated method (it shows 122.2, 131.0, 115.1, 85.7 and 79.4 for the same five records), so the raw column is the right one, as the notes say. Other FishBase L. gibbosus records: 10-g fish 180 and 290 mg O2/kg/h at 25 and 30 °C (routine); a 44.92-g fish at 20 °C, standard 45.0 and active 408 (main ref. Thurston & Gehrke 1993 for the standard record). A FB4 manual page image used for the equation is saved as docs/research_notes/fetched/v2/Altman_Dittmer_1971.fb4guide_p14.png.
